thread:
Sara: Heads-up — after last night's FP8 rollout on dedicated-west we saw a regression on a subset of latency-sensitive routes. p95 climbed ~40ms on some batches. attaching profiler link: https://perf.redwood/runs/1751112219 :eyes:

Raja: Can you paste the quick perf snippet? is this only with our new per-channel calibration tables or also with the per-tensor fallback?

Sara: Quick dump below from the canary cluster (same model, quantized with per-channel calibrations):
```
2025-11-08 03:12:10 INFO serving: batch_size=4 seq=1024 mode=stream
p50=18ms p95=112ms p99=184ms throughput=220 tok/s
(after FP8 rollback on same node) p50=17ms p95=74ms p99=120ms throughput=340 tok/s
```

Dong: Hmm that's a pretty significant drop in throughput. Any kernel selection changes in compile that could cause a slower code-path for mid-size batches?

Sara: We did enable an FP8 fused attention kernel variant that prefers per-channel scales (more memory ops). The runtime should switch to an INT8-ish path for seq<128 but picks FP8 kernel for longer seq.

Ana: Could this be KV-cache warmup alignment? I remember a mismatch where prefix-preserving sampling caused more KV misses, which exploded memory copies. Behavior would appear worse for long seqs.

Kevin: I pulled the trace — the stall is in 'kv_prefetch_memcpy' and a subsequent `launch_attention_kernel` that shows ~2x launch latency variance. Link: https://perf.redwood/flame/1751112219

Raja: So multiple hypotheses: (1) FP8 per-channel causes extra memory bandwidth (scale arrays per-row), (2) kernel selection heuristic picks a slower fused kernel for some sequence/batch combos, (3) sampler produced more tail-heavy sequences exposing kv cache miss rate. We should triage in parallel.

perfbot: @Sara opened perf ticket PERF-4521 and kicked off nightly microbench with binomial sampler + fixed seed to reproduce.

Sara: For experiment plan: I want to run three controlled runs on canary: A) per-tensor calibration (fast path) B) per-channel calibration but with kernel heuristic pinned to legacy FP8 kernel C) per-channel full with our new sampler but prefetch warmup disabled. Keep batch size/seq distro identical.

Dong: Add a version that forces 'compile.use_dynamic_kernels=false' so we can see if compile-time routing is the root cause. Also log nvprof counters: l2_read_transactions, dram_read_bytes.

Ana: I'll check the calibration dataset too — we recently switched to tail-amplified sampling (more long prompts) for the calibration set which might have biased per-channel scales. If extreme outliers exist they can blow up per-channel multipliers and change effective sparsity. Suggest clipping the extreme 0.1% during calibration and re-run.

Kevin: Good call. If per-channel has few outliers, kernel may allocate different temporary buffers. I can run a quick script to compute per-channel scale percentiles across the calibration corpus.

Sara: Minimal reproduction action items: 1) Dong: microbench with dynamic_kernels=false + nvprof 2) Kevin: per-channel scale percentiles + top-100 outlier examples 3) Ana: re-run calibration with 0.1% clipping 4) Raja: patch runtime heuristic to prefer legacy kernel for seq in [512,1536] for one experiment.

Raja: I'll prepare a small canary flag so we can A/B without a full rollback. If we confirm it's kernel selection, we can revert selection policy quickly.

Sara: Thanks. If anyone sees a quick mitigation we can toggle, ping on this thread and I'll flip canary. :thumbsup:

Kevin: I ran a quick pass — per-channel scale 99.9th percentile is 12x median on our calibration set (tail-heavy). Uploading top examples to the perf ticket.

Ana: Recalibrate with clipping=0.001 applied to per-channel scales — early results look promising: p95 back to ~78ms on a small canary run. Will run full microbench tonight.

Dong: If clipping helps, we should update the calibration docs and add an automated outlier detector in the cal pipeline (warn on >8x median).

Sara: Agreed. Let's treat this as 'sampler + per-channel interaction' rather than a pure kernel bug until we confirm. Closing loop after microbench results.

perfbot: NIGHTLY-MICROBENCH RESULTS (run 1751112345): A: per-tensor p95=76ms, B: per-channel (pinned-legacy-kernel) p95=79ms, C: per-channel (new-kernel) p95=113ms — full logs at https://perf.redwood/runs/1751112345

Raja: That's pretty telling. New kernel + per-channel = regress. Next steps: either patch kernel to be more memory-friendly or tighten calibration sampling to avoid extreme scales.

Sara: Great work everyone — let's reconvene tomorrow after Kevin and Ana finish full corpus runs.
